channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Titans placed WR Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve.
item.description: He’ll miss at least the next four games. Even in moderate-sized leagues, Robinson is likely a cut candidate at this point given how his playing time and target share have been reduced. This should help out Carnell Tate (once he returns from his shoulder injury) and Elic Ayomanor in the target department.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Ravens released K Harrison Mevis from the practice squad.
item.description: He’ll be free to ply his wares again as it appears Riley Patterson has taken hold of the Ravens’ kicking gig. Mevis, 24, will continue to wander the kicking tryout circuit for another chance.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Dolphins placed DT Jordan Phillips (biceps) on injured reserve.
item.description: He tore his biceps and will miss the remainder of the season. The 2025 fifth-rounder — and notably not the older defensive tackle also named Jordan Phillips — had played 326 snaps this year with a 57.4 PFF grade as an interior lineman.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) is “trending in the right direction” of playing on Thursday Night.
item.description: Montgomery should see the vast majority of the Texans run attack volume if he’s able to go, relegating Emari Demercado back to the bench outside of a few third-down plays here or there. It’s hard to trust that anything good will come of this given how the team has played this year, but Montgomery on volume would fit in as a low-end RB2 on a week with six teams on bye.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the team expects TJ Hockenson (wrist/chest) “to progress” ahead of Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
item.description: We’ll be monitoring practice participation for Hockenson after he missed all three practices last week. Should he miss another game, Gavin Bartholomew caught a touchdown in his absence and would be a reasonable TE2.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Commanders designated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) to return from injured reserve.
item.description: Ben Standig reports that he’s expecting Croskey-Merritt to be active for Monday night barring a setback. We’re expecting a pass-happy Commanders offense as they try to keep pace with Cincinnati’s high-flying offense, but given how many teams are on bye there’s certainly worse FLEX starts out there than a returning “Bill.”-Rivers McCown

item.title: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Luther Burden III has cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol.
item.description: Burden had the Bears’ bye week to recover from the head injury, and it looks like he’ll be a full go for Week 11 against the Saints — barring a setback, of course. Burden has been an elite producer of late, piling up 283 receiving yards over his past three outings while being targeted on a strong 30 percent of his pass routes. Burden over that span has averaged nearly 11 yards after the catch per reception, the third highest mark in the NFL.-Denny Carter

item.title: David Montgomery (groin) was seen practicing Tuesday.
item.description: Montgomery looks to be in line for a full workload in Thursday night’s game against the Colts, who have struggled mightily against the rush in recent weeks. Woody Marks, who sustained a concussion in Week 10 against the Browns, will very likely miss Thursday night as he works through the league’s concussion protocol. Montgomery will be a floor-based RB2/3 against the Colts.-Denny Carter

item.title: Texans placed Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) on injured reserve.
item.description: Al-Shaair has been playing through a serious groin issue for weeks. He was sidelined in Week 10 against the Browns and will now miss extended time. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander said Al-Shaair is “likely to miss more than four games but has not been ruled out for the season.” The Texans this season have allowed the 13th highest EPA per play and the tenth lowest offensive success rate. Their defense will be a little more vulnerable with Al-Shaair sidelined.-Denny Carter

item.title: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’s “hopeful” Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman, Jr. (foot) can return in Week 11.
item.description: Wilson and Pittman, after being sidelined for about a month, could return to a Steelers offense in desperate need of pass-catching help. Before his finger injury, Wilson was interesting for fantasy purposes, seeing 14 percent of the team’s targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards with a solid 23 percent targets per route rate. Pittman, meanwhile, was targeted on a lowly 13 percent of his routes over the season’s first few games. Their return could be a major issue for Germie Bernard, who’s had three straight quiet games, including a zero in Week 10 against the Bengals. Bernard won’t be playable in 12-team formats when Wilson returns to action.-Denny Carter
